**Finding: IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data — compliant (no redline).**

The bargain in § 4, read with § 5(b), § 8 and § 11(c), clears the fallback and most of the preferred position:

- **Deliverables vest in us.** § 4(a) makes all Works "the property of Company"; § 11(c) (p0044) adds an express assignment of right, title and interest in Works in progress on termination after final payment. Ownership (subject only to the paid-invoice condition, which is the rule's own premise) subsumes the fallback's perpetual/irrevocable/worldwide/royalty-free use, modify and sublicense elements, and § 4(d) confirms we may modify the software and engage others to do so without further payment.
- **Vendor retention is properly bounded.** § 4(b)(i)–(ii) limits Contractor's retained ownership to its own pre-existing tools, methodologies, know-how and administrative records — permitted generic-tools retention, not a deliverables grab. No joint ownership is created anywhere.
- **Embedded Vendor IP is licensed back.** § 4(c) is royalty-free, perpetual and sublicensable for our business operations.
- **Customer Data.** There is no Vendor licence in our data to narrow: § 8 bars Contractor from any use or disclosure without our prior written permission (a consent-gated prohibition, not a standing licence), and § 5(b) carves out "rights respecting programs, data and materials provided by Company."

Preferred-only shortfalls noted, not flagged: the § 4(c) licence is perpetual but not expressly "irrevocable," and there is no standalone Customer Data ownership sentence (achieved in substance by § 8 and § 5(b)). Both are candidates if the agreement is reopened for other reasons.
